_readme: Researched jack layouts, one entry per pedal, imported by import-pedal-jacks.js.
SIDES ARE BOARD-RELATIVE, viewed from above with the player at the front:
top    = the rear edge, furthest from the player (BOSS calls this the 'rear panel')
bottom = the front edge, nearest the player
left / right = the long sides. A guitar plugs into the RIGHT of a standard
BOSS compact, and signal leaves to the LEFT, which is why boards
are wired right to left.
THE MIRRORING TRAP: a manual that draws the REAR PANEL face-on shows it as seen
from behind the pedal, so its left and right are flipped relative to the top-down
view used here. Where a source only offers that view and nothing else disambiguates,
the entry is confidence 'unknown' rather than a guess.
positionPercent is approximate, read off the panel diagram. It places the cable
endpoint along an edge: 0 = rear/left end, 100 = front/right end. Exactness is not
required and must not hold up an otherwise good entry.
confidence 'confirmed' = every recorded jack's edge was read off sourceUrl.
confidence 'unknown'   = researched and NOT confirmable; jacks MUST be empty, and
routing falls back to its default assumption.
SOURCES. sourceUrl is normally a manufacturer manual or panel diagram. It may
also be the token 'owner-inspection', meaning the edges were read off the
physical pedal by the board's owner - better evidence than a drawing, since it
cannot be a different revision and cannot fall foul of the mirroring trap. See
supabase/migrations/20260801000003_jacks_owner_inspection.sql.
A jack nobody observed is OMITTED, not guessed. Entries sourced by inspection
may therefore be missing rows - typically the DC jack - and that is a smaller
lie than inventing an edge for it.

pedals.name: AW-3
pedals.notes: BOSS compact enclosure. Connector list quoted from this pedal's own product-page Specifications. Edges follow the compact-series panel layout - OUTPUTs on the LEFT, INPUTs on the RIGHT, control/expression jack on the right below the input, DC IN on the rear - which was read directly off the panel diagrams in the DD-7, OC-5 and PH-3 manuals and is corroborated by the original seed data for CS-3, DS-1, NS-2, TU-3, RC-1, RV-6 and SD-1. Two DEDICATED inputs, GUITAR IN and BASS IN, rather than one INPUT - which an assumed layout would have got wrong.

pedals.name: NS-2
pedals.notes: BOSS compact. CORRECTED 2026-08-01 from the owner's own unit: SEND is on the LEFT, not the right. The original entry put input, send AND return all on the right by applying the compact-series rule 'OUTPUTs left, INPUTs right' to the jack NAMES rather than their function - but SEND is an output (signal leaves for the loop) and RETURN is an input (it comes back), so by that entry's own rule send belonged on the left. The Roland manual (https://static.roland.com/assets/media/pdf/NS-2_e01_W.pdf) remains the source for the connector LIST; the edges are the owner's. This matters more than most: the NS-2 is the hub pedal on both real boards, so its send and return are where the whole loop attaches.

pedals.name: PW-3
pedals.notes: Jacks are on the REAR face, not the long sides - unusual for a wah, and the reason this pedal was initially recorded as unknown. Owner's Manual 'Panel Descriptions' shows that face head-on: INPUT (4) at one end, the GUITAR/BASS switch (5), DC IN (6), OUTPUT (7) at the other. That view looks AT the rear panel, so its left and right are mirrored relative to the top-down view used here; mirrored, INPUT lands on the right and OUTPUT on the left. The manual's connection illustration independently agrees - the electric guitar feeds the right-hand side and the amp is fed from the left. Two views agreeing is what moved this from unknown to confirmed.

pedals.name: BigSky
pedals.notes: User Manual "Rear Panel" section lists POWER, MIDI, INPUTS (LEFT/RIGHT), OUTPUTS (LEFT/RIGHT) and EXP together - every jack is on the rear edge, which is what makes this one of the few pedals rotation could ever help. Use LEFT for mono, per the manual.

pedals.name: Timeline
pedals.notes: User Manual "Rear Panel" section lists POWER, MIDI, INPUTS (LEFT/RIGHT), OUTPUTS (LEFT/RIGHT) and EXP together - every jack is on the rear edge, which is what makes this one of the few pedals rotation could ever help. RIGHT IN doubles as the feedback-loop return and RIGHT OUT as its send, per the same section.

pedals.name: Aqua-Puss
pedals.notes: Smalls enclosure. The manufacturer product photograph shows the top edge reading, left to right: OUT, +9VDC, IN - so output left, DC centre, input right, all on the rear edge. The owner reported the same signal layout from their own unit before the photo was found, and the two agree; the DC jack comes from the photo, which is why it is recorded now and was omitted before. Top-edge signal jacks make this pedal rotation-eligible.

pedals.name: Conspiracy Theory
pedals.notes: Smalls enclosure. The manufacturer product photograph shows the top edge reading, left to right: OUT, +9VDC, IN - so output left, DC centre, input right, all on the rear edge. The owner reported the same signal layout from their own unit before the photo was found, and the two agree; the DC jack comes from the photo, which is why it is recorded now and was omitted before. Top-edge signal jacks make this pedal rotation-eligible.

pedals.name: Flint
pedals.notes: V2. Owner reports EVERY jack is on the TOP (rear) edge, with input to the right and output to the left - matching the BigSky and Timeline entries, whose rear panels were read off Strymon's own manuals. Stereo: the product page lists 'low impedance independent TS stereo outputs (left and right)' and a single 'high impedance TRS stereo audio input', so two output rows and one input row. EXP and POWER are on the same edge; their positions along it are approximate, which the positionPercent contract permits - the edge is what was observed. USB is not modelled as a jack type.

pedals.name: Chorus Ensemble Deluxe
pedals.notes: CE-1 clone in a LANDSCAPE 1590BB. The manufacturer product photograph shows two jack barrels on the LEFT edge beside a vertical 'mono stereo output' label, one on the RIGHT edge labelled 'Input', and '9V (-)+' printed on the face by the top edge for the DC jack. The owner reported input right / output left independently and the photo agrees; the SECOND (stereo) output and the DC jack come from the photo, so both are recorded now. Ordinary side-jack layout, so rotation would only move the jacks off the sides.
